16. Mr. Faqueer Shahabuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants argues that there is no eye witness of the occurrence and the conviction is based solely on a dying declaration of Merajuddin, which according to defence was not genuine and true. He further argues that another dying declaration was recorded by C.O. (Dev) which has been wit held by the prosecution, for which adverse presumption should have been drawn against the prosecution. 

 29. It is in evidence of P.W. 14 that Merajuddin died shortly after he recorded .his dying declaration and that the CO. (Dev) came after recording of dying declaration by him. Except P.W. 14 no other witness has said anything about recording of dying declaration by the C.O. None of the parties has examined the C.O. as a witness. In that view of the matter, there is no force in the contention of the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants that non-production of the dying declaration recorded by C.O. (Dev) is very material or the Court should have drawn adverse „presumption Against the prosecution for such non-production.
